Roda L. Tajon has advised three theses in this repository, all of which were completed in 2024. Their research supervision covers a diverse range of sub-topics, including mental health and well-being, gender and inclusion, culture and identity, arts and creative practice, and educational technology. Based on the available data, Tajon's supervision patterns show a focus on contemporary cultural phenomena, particularly within the context of music and digital media.

In 2024, Tajon advised a technical report by Francelle Joanne C. Bacud titled "All Kinds of Blue: Exploring the Emotional Effect of Lucy's Blue Album on Selected Filipino Fans' Mental Well-Being." This work utilized a qualitative approach to investigate how the South Korean band LUCY’s second EP, BLUE, impacts the mental and emotional states of selected Filipino fans. This indicates an interest in the intersection of music consumption and mental health and well-being.

During the same year, Tajon supervised Airiel Licca Depante’s thesis, "#MOOTOO: An Exploratory Study on Mamamoo as Purveyor of Feminism Ideals." This research examined the intersection of K-pop and feminist discourse within the patriarchal context of South Korean society, specifically looking at female empowerment. This work falls under the sub-topic of gender and inclusion.

Tajon also advised a practice-based multimedia project titled "Project TALA: A Virtual Exhibit Prototype Celebrating P-Pop, Philippine History and Culture, and Historical and Cultural Advocacy in Web Virtual Reality (VR)." This project, which covers the sub-topics of culture and identity, arts and creative practice, and educational technology, developed a Web Virtual Reality (VR) exhibit prototype. The project aims to use "edutainment"—a blend of education and entertainment—to engage younger audiences by promoting Philippine history, arts, and culture through the lens of P-Pop.

While Tajon has supervised three students in 2024, there is no evidence of any advisees in 2026, which is the latest year containing any items in this repository. Tajon has no articles of their own currently listed in this repository. The breadth of topics supervised suggests a capacity for guiding research that connects popular culture, such as K-pop and P-Pop, with academic discourses in psychology, sociology, and digital technology. Evidence regarding Tajon's specific academic degrees or formal institutional affiliations is not provided in the fact sheet. Their supervision style appears to accommodate both qualitative investigative studies and practice-based multimedia development.
